repository_card.frontier: Both manuscript packages are frozen. The current paper concerns characteristic-free finite span bounds and sharp Gauss-fibre examples; no directly matching weekly Gauss-fibre theorem was verified.
repository_card.bridge_hypothesis: Compare fundamental-form symmetry with the paper's tangent-absorption condition. Dictionary: first fundamental data -> tangent space; higher forms -> osculating restrictions. General-point infinitesimal symmetry loses special finite incidence and cannot extend a characteristic-free theorem by itself.
repository_card.next_finite_task: For one existing sharp example, compute first and second fundamental forms and compare their ranks with the point-span bound. Use the Hodge split-binary family only as a candidate example family after checking smoothness and tangent ranks.
repository_card.falsifier: Reject an extension if it relies on characteristic-zero genericity, identifies tangent and second-osculating contact, or infers a special absorbing point set from an automorphism-dimension bound.
repository_card.proposal_status: speculative; not executed or formally verified

sources.title: Fundamental forms and infinitesimal symmetries of projective varieties
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.source_claim: Hwang and Li bound the dimension of the linear automorphism group of a projective variety using fundamental forms at a general point, with equality characterized by Euler symmetry.
sources.limits: A general-point symmetry bound does not construct a special finite tangent-absorbing configuration. Higher fundamental forms and the characteristic assumptions must be retained. First posted 9 August.

sources.title: A note on the noncommutative Hodge conjecture for graded matrix factorizations
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.review_depth: v1: Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.2, Lemma 3.1 and Proposition 4.1
sources.source_claim: Lin and Zhang report rational Hodge results for sums of independently very general squarefree binary forms, with m>=2 and d>=7. Explicit matrix factorizations supply classes; monodromy controls their exhaustion.
sources.limits: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 concern this particular very-general family. They do not settle general rational Hodge, identify every special parameter, or construct the repository's prescribed clean-nodal detector.
